body.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), let
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}=P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\) be any regular conditional law of
the complete causal-data array given the realized query, define
\[
 \mu_{P,s}(z_0)=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]
 \quad\text{(the same value for every \(i\))},
 \qquad
 \Sigma_P(z_0)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0),
\]
and retain the regression label \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S)\).  Then, for
\(P\)-almost every admissible query value under its marginal query law, the
labelled point
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)=\bigl(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,
                         \Sigma_P(z_0)\bigr)
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  The common-replica equality
in the first display follows from \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering}.
No membership assertion is made for the bare kernel \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\),
or for a chosen conditional version at a query-null value.
body.justification: Disintegration transfers exactly the active support, centering, conditional-design, independence, and covariance clauses to the labelled tuple \(\xi_P(z_0)\).
body.gap: No conditional version is selected at a query-null value.
body.consumer: Every causal upper transfer uses the labelled tuple rather than a bare kernel.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\) and a regular conditional law
\(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}=P(\,\cdot\mid z_0)\).  Define
\[
 \mu_{P,s}(z_0)=\mathbb E_P[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0],
 \qquad
 \Sigma_P(z_0)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Z_j\mid z_0),            \tag{1}
\]
and retain \(m=(m_1,\ldots,m_S)\).  Bounded wealth makes the first quantity
finite.  Assumption \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} says that its
value is common across replicas \(i\), and it gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}
 =\mu_{P,s}(z_0).                                             \tag{2}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:consistency} disintegrates to
\(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}=B_{si}(1)\) almost surely under the kernel, and
\texttt{ass:event-date-transport} gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}B_{si}(0)=m_s(z_{0s}).         \tag{3}
\]
Thus (2)--(3) verify the common mean label, consistency, and transport
clauses of \texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}.

Let \(\mathcal X=\sigma((X_{uv})_{u,v})\).  The two conditional-mean
equalities in \texttt{ass:design-conditional-centering} become, under the
regular conditional law,
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}[Q_{sti}\mid\mathcal X]
 =m_s(X_{st}),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 [B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid\mathcal X]
 =\mu_{P,s}(z_0).                                             \tag{4}
\]
These are mean restrictions only.  They impose neither identical replica
distributions nor independence between training and event coordinates of a
unit history.  Assumption \texttt{ass:cross-unit-independence} becomes
conditional independence of the histories across \((s,i)\) given
\(\mathcal X\) under \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\).

The boundedness, exact-observation, and interior assertions disintegrate to
kernel-almost-sure assertions outside a marginally null set.  Holder
membership is a property of the retained labels.  Assumptions
\texttt{ass:design-density} and \texttt{ass:temporal-mixing} give, on a
marginally conull set,
\[
 c_X\le f_{st\mid z_0}(x)\le C_X
 \quad\text{for Lebesgue-almost every \(x\)},
 \qquad
 \beta_s(k\mid z_0)\le\beta_0\rho_0^k                       \tag{5}
\]
for every \(s,t\) and every integer \(k\ge1\).

Assumptions \texttt{ass:donor-independence} and
\texttt{ass:donor-training-separation} give, under the kernel, i.i.d. donors
independent of the complete joint panel.  Donor unbiasedness, ellipticity,
the fourth-moment condition, and (1) give
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}Z_j=z_0,
 \qquad c_\Sigma I_{Sd}\preceq\Sigma_P(z_0)\preceq C_\Sigma I_{Sd}, \tag{6}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_{P,z_0}}
 \|\Sigma_P(z_0)^{-1/2}(Z_j-z_0)\|_2^4\le B^4.              \tag{7}
\]
The lower eigenvalue \(c_\Sigma>0\) makes the inverse square root in (7)
well defined.

There are finitely many cohorts, dates, and replicas, and countably many
lags.  Intersecting the conull query sets supporting (2)--(7) and the
disintegrated support assertions therefore leaves a marginally conull set.
At every query in it, the labelled tuple
\[
 \xi_P(z_0)=\bigl(\mathbb K_{P,z_0};\mu_P(z_0),m,
                         \Sigma_P(z_0)\bigr)                 \tag{8}
\]
satisfies every member property in
\texttt{def:fixed-query-kernel-class}; hence
\(\xi_P(z_0)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  Equation (8), not the
bare law \(\mathbb K_{P,z_0}\), is the well-typed class member.  Nothing is
asserted about an arbitrarily selected conditional version on the
complementary null set.
